quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a car's headlights are blinding you, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car has its high beams on, look away from the headlights. Look toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When must you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling helps other drivers know your intentions and prevents accidents.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed constant on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp. Once you move onto the exit ramp, then slow down.

questions.question: Where must you remove snow and ice from your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to remove all snow and ice from your vehicle before driving. Fines may apply if you do not follow this rule.

questions.question: When can you continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light changes to yellow, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This circular sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is ahead. Watch for trains and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This diamond-shaped yellow sign warns drivers of hazards. It tells you that the road may be slippery when wet, making your vehicle harder to control. Drive with extra care.

questions.question: What must a driver do when entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Assume that other drivers will move lanes for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: You must yield to drivers already on the interstate. Merge safely when there is an opening in traffic.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for an approaching train.
Wait for a flagger's signal before proceeding, if one is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Listen for trains and obey any flagger at the crossing.

questions.question: After you stop for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not go until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep going unless there are already cars or people in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going unless there are already cars or people in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and cars already in the intersection go first. You can continue, but slow down if the light might change before you get there.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign is always a stop sign. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: The bigger a vehicle is, the bigger its blind spots are. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that you cannot see in the side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: When you turn or change lanes, you must:

options.text: Always use your signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
Signal only if other cars are nearby.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
questions.explanation: Always use your signal when changing lanes, turning, or leaving a curb. Do not skip this step—it is the law and a safe driving habit.

questions.question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Let cars on the public road go first.
Assume other drivers will move lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cars on the public road go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, let cars on the public road go first. Merge safely into traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the correct lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Use your signal and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes, then back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make sudden last-minute turns. If you are not in the right lane for your turn, drive to the next intersection and make your turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot push water away from the road as well. If you go too fast, your tires may lose grip and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A four-way intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, let other cars go first, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly so you can check the traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other cars go first, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and enter at the same speed as the traffic around you. Always let other cars go first when entering a roadway.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign intersection. What should happen?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Let the driver on your right go first at a four-way stop if you both arrive at the same time. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may go if the road is clear.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you pass these signs, you are going the wrong way. This can cause a head-on collision. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down should be your first action when you cannot see well. This helps you stay safe on bad road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet makes roads slippery. Safety may require you to drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: A driver under 21 with a probationary license can transport dependents and how many other passengers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Up to one other passenger.
questions.explanation: Drivers with probationary licenses have restrictions. Drivers under 21 can only transport dependents plus one other passenger.

questions.question: What should you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming?

options.text: Stop immediately and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road safely and stop.
Slow down and let it pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road safely and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road as far as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. This applies no matter which direction the emergency vehicle is coming from.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to create more distance.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to spot tailgaters. If someone is following too close, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, move to the curb or side of the road right away and stop.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that cars are backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the right side and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. If cars are backing up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull off and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when bad conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn with red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other. Only proceed when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: Under ideal driving conditions, a driver should maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Use the Three-Second rule to maintain safe following distance. When the car ahead passes an object, count three seconds before you reach that same object. This means you are following safely. Increase your distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Under normal driving conditions, a motorist should grip the steering wheel at:
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock.
questions.explanation: Think of the steering wheel as a clock face. For normal driving, grip the outside rim at 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock. Keep your thumbs along the rim of the wheel.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train sounds. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of low clearance on the overpass ahead. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (in this case, 13 feet, 6 inches).

questions.question: On a two-lane street, your vehicle is being followed by a fire engine that is not using its emergency signals. You should:

options.text: Continue to drive in a normal manner.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move as far to the right as possible, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to drive in a normal manner.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle behind you is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No less safe than driving under any other conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very risky. It endangers you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers. Keeping your attention on driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: While backing, you should:

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look out the rear window while backing. Do not depend only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: From top to bottom, the proper order for traffic lights is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is on top and green is on the bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: When driving, you must turn your headlights on:

options.text: When you turn your wipers on.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use headlights from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise. Also use them when you cannot see 500 feet ahead and whenever your windshield wipers are on.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. If there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead pass through, you:

options.text: May go through the intersection without stopping again.
Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before going. Do not skip this stop just because other vehicles did.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep the steering wheel straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the steering wheel straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slowly remove your foot from the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control. Once the car is steady, brake gently and pull over to a safe spot.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Move to the right side and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, move safely to the right side of the road and stop. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear path. In heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can pull over.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well in the dark. Other drivers' headlights can blind you. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When flashing signals warn of a train, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Look and listen for trains. A lowered gate or the sound of a train also means a train is coming.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right. Then you may go when it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:

options.text: Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, whether or not there is a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: If a collision cannot be avoided, you should:

options.text: Hit something that gives way rather than something hard.
Hit something standing still rather than something moving toward you.
Hit with a glancing blow or sideswipe if you must hit anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a collision, hit something that gives way like bushes rather than something hard. Hit something stationary rather than something moving toward you. A glancing blow or sideswipe causes less damage than a head-on crash.
